charts.title: Average percentage of the population engaged in sports, exercise, and recreation per day in the United States from 2010 to 2022
charts.short: Percentage of U.S. population engaged in sports and exercise per day 2010-2022
charts.description: In 2022, it was found that 21.2 percent of men in the United States participated in sports, exercise, and recreational activities daily, compared to only 19.1 percent of women. These statistics highlight a notable difference in the daily engagement of different genders in sporting activities. Other factors influencing this participation include socioeconomic status, age, disability, ethnicity, geography, personal interests, and societal expectations. charts.title: Average amount of time spent on leisure and sports by U.S. civilian population from 2009 to 2022 (in hours per day)
charts.short: Hours per day spent on leisure and sports by U.S. population 2009-2022
charts.description: This graph depicts the average hours per day spent by the U.S. civilian population on sports and leisure activities from 2009 to 2022. Men spent an average of 5.58 hours per day on sports and leisure in 2022.
charts.note: United States; 2009 to 2022; aprox. 8,100 (2022); 15 years and older

charts.title: Average amount of time spent on sports, exercise, and recreation in the United States from 2009 to 2022 (hours per day)
charts.short: Hours per day spent on sports, exercise, and recreation in the U.S. 2009-2022
charts.description: When surveyed in 2022, it was found that the civilian population of the United States spent an average of 0.29 hours per day on sports, exercise, and recreation. In total, this was a decrease from the previous year owing to the drop off among men from 0.4 to 0.33 hours, however, among women the figure rose slightly in 2022 from 0.24 to 0.25 hours.

charts.title: Percentage of adults that were physically inactive in the United States from 2017-2020, by state
charts.short: Percentage of physically inactive U.S. adults by state 2017-2020
charts.description: This statistic represents the percentage of adults in the United States that have done no physical activity or exercise within the preceding 30 days, from 2017 to 2020. During this time, Mississippi had the highest rate of physical inactivity among U.S. states with 33.2 percent of adults reporting no physical activity or exercise besides their job. The state of Colorado had the lowest rates of physical inactivity at this time.
charts.note: United States; 2017-2020; 18 years and older

charts.title: Leading outdoor activities in the United States in 2022, by number of participants (in millions)
charts.short: Most popular outdoor activities in the U.S. 2022
charts.description: Hiking was the most popular outdoor activity amongst people in the United States in 2022, accounting for nearly 60 million participants. The second most popular outdoor sport in the North American country was running, jogging, and trail running with 56.9 million participants during the same year.

charts.title: Share of participants in outdoor activities in the United States in 2023, by generation
charts.short: Outdoor participation rate in the U.S. 2023, by generation
charts.description: According to a survey, about six out of ten U.S. Americans who were born from 1980 onwards participated in at least one outdoor activity in 2023. The outdoor participation rate was not as high in older generations that year, with 45.3 percent of individuals born between 1945 and 1964 from the U.S. participating in outdoor sports in 2023.
